title.raw: 卷83 晉紀五

value.zh: 眭誇 馮亮 鄭修 崔廓 子賾 徐則 張文詡
value.en: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, Cui Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu
value.literal: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, his son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu

value.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。
value.en: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit was overwhelmed.
value.literal: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit lost itself.

value.zh: 若乃理高《象系》，管輅思而不解；
value.en: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;
value.literal: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;

value.zh: 事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。
value.en: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated them yet could not exhaust them.
value.literal: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust them.

value.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。
value.en: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, and dragon pattern has no equal.
value.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing, the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, dragon pattern has no equal.

value.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚；
value.en: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;
value.literal: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;

value.zh: 郢客之奏《陽春》，誰能赴節？
value.en: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?
value.literal: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?

value.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道邁于東平，文藝高於北海。
value.en: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.
value.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.

value.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。
value.en: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
value.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

value.zh: 雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。
value.en: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my humble dust, the path between us is far and still.
value.literal: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my clear dust, the path between us is far and still.

value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 三年春正月丁丑，罷秦州，并雍州。
value.en: Taikang 3, spring, first month, dingchou: Qin province was abolished and merged into Yong province.
value.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on the day dingchou, Qin province was abolished and merged into Yong.

value.zh: 甲午，以尚書張華都督幽州諸軍事。
value.en: Jiawu: Zhang Hua, a master of writing, was appointed commander of all military affairs in You province.
value.literal: On the day jiawu Zhang Hua of the masters of writing was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of You province.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 永康元年春正月癸亥朔，大赦，改元。
value.en: The new moon of the first month of Yongkang brought a general amnesty and a new reign title.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, spring, first month, on the guihai new moon, a general amnesty; the era name was changed.

value.zh: 己卯，日有蝕之。
value.en: The sun was eclipsed on the jimao day.
value.literal: On the jimao day, there was a solar eclipse.

value.zh: 丙子，皇孫𧇃卒。
value.en: On the bingzi day the imperial grandson died.
value.literal: On the bingzi day, the imperial grandson 𧇃 died.

value.zh: 夏四月辛卯，日有蝕之。
value.en: Another solar eclipse occurred on the xinmao day in the fourth month.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinmao day, there was a solar eclipse.

value.zh: 癸巳，梁王肜、趙王倫矯詔廢賈后爲庶人，司空張華、尚書僕射裴頠皆遇害，侍中賈謐及黨與數十人皆伏誅。
value.en: On the guisi day Princes Xiong and Lun forged an edict that deposed Empress Jia; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were killed, and Jia Mi with dozens of his partisans went to the execution ground.
value.literal: On the guisi day, Prince Xiong of Liang and Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict deposing Empress Jia to commoner status; Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei both met harm and died; Palace Attendant Jia Mi and several tens of his faction were all executed.

value.zh: 甲午，倫矯詔大赦，自爲相國、都督中外諸軍，如宣文輔魏故事，追復故皇太子位。
value.en: The next day Prince Lun forged a general amnesty, named himself chancellor and commander-in-chief on the model of Sima Yi and Sima Zhao, and posthumously reinstated the murdered crown prince.
value.literal: On the jiawu day, Lun forged an edict for a general amnesty, made himself chancellor of state and area commander for all military affairs within and without, according to the old precedent of Xuan and Wen assisting Wei, and posthumously restored the former crown prince’s position.

value.zh: 丁酉，以梁王肜爲太宰，左光祿大夫何劭爲司徒，右光祿大夫劉寔爲司空，淮南王允爲驃騎將軍。
value.en: Prince Xiong became grand steward, He Shao minister of education, Liu Shi minister of works, and Prince Yun of Huainan general of agile cavalry on the dingyou day.
value.literal: On the dingyou day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward; Left Household Grandee He Shao was made minister of education; Right Household Grandee Liu Shi was made minister of works; Prince Yun of Huainan was made general of agile cavalry.

value.zh: 己亥，趙王倫矯詔害賈庶人于金墉城。
value.en: On the jihai day Prince Lun had the deposed Empress Jia killed inside the Jinyong fortress.
value.literal: On the jihai day, Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict and harmed the commoner Jia at the Jinyong Fortress.

value.zh: 六年春正月，大赦。
value.en: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: In spring, in the first month of the sixth year, there was a great amnesty.

value.zh: 司空、下邳王晃薨。
value.en: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Minister of Works, died.
value.literal: Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Minister of Works, died.

value.zh: 以中書監張華爲司空，太尉、隴西王泰爲尚書令，衛將軍、梁王肜爲太子太保。
value.en: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Works; Sima Tai, Prince of Longxi and Grand Commandant, became Director of the Secretariat; and Sima Rong, Prince of Liang and General of the Guards, became Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
value.literal: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works; Tai, Prince of Longxi and Grand Commandant, was made Director of the Secretariat; Rong, Prince of Liang and General of the Guards, was made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 丁丑，地震。
value.en: On dingchou, an earthquake occurred.
value.literal: On dingchou, there was an earthquake.

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 永康元年三月，中台星坼，太白晝見。
value.en: Yongkang 1’s third month saw the asterism of the high ministers fracture while Venus shone in daylight.
value.literal: In the third month of Yongkang 1 the central terrace stars split, and the Great White appeared by day.

value.zh: 占曰：「台星失常，三公憂。
value.en: The prognostication said, "When the Terrace Stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes will have anxiety.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When terrace stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes grieve.

value.zh: 太白晝見，為不臣。」
value.en: When Venus appears by day, it means disloyal ministers."
value.literal: The Great White seen by daylight means disloyal subjects.

value.zh: 是月，賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺後，斬司空張華。
value.en: That month Empress Jia slew the heir; Sima Lun rapidly ousted and killed her and executed Zhang Hua.
value.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir apparent; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered the empress and beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua.

value.zh: 其五月，熒惑入南斗。
value.en: The fifth month brought Mars into the Southern Dipper.
value.literal: That fifth month Spark-Delight entered the Southern Dipper.

value.zh: 占曰：「宰相死，兵大起。
value.en: The prognostication said, "The chancellor will die, and war will greatly arise.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The chief minister will die; troops rise on a grand scale.

value.zh: 斗，又吳分野。」
value.en: Dipper is also Wu’s allotment."
value.literal: The Dipper also marks Wu’s celestial field.

value.zh: 是時，趙王倫為相，明年，篡位，三王興師誅之。
value.en: Sima Lun held the premiership, seized the throne the following year, then fell to princely coalitions.
value.literal: At that time Prince Zhao Lun was chancellor; the next year he usurped the throne, and princes raised armies and executed him.

value.zh: 太安二年，石冰破揚州。
value.en: Tai’an 2 saw Shi Bing overrun Yangzhou.
value.literal: In the second year of Tai’an Shi Bing captured Yangzhou.

value.zh: 其八月，熒惑入箕。
value.en: That August Mars entered the Winnowing Basket.
value.literal: That eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Winnowing Basket.

value.zh: 占曰：「人主失位，兵起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The ruler of men loses his position, and war arises."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler loses his throne; troops arise.

value.zh: 明年趙王倫篡位，改元。
value.en: The following year Sima Lun seized the throne and altered the reign title.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne and changed the era name.

value.zh: 二年二月，太白出西方，逆行入東井。
value.en: The second year’s second month brought Venus out in the west, retrograding into the Eastern Well.
value.literal: In the second month of the second year the Great White emerged in the west and moved retrograde into the Eastern Well.

value.zh: 占曰：「國失政，大臣為亂。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The state loses its government, and great ministers make disorder."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.

value.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫，倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢，明年，誅死。
value.en: Prince Qi’s coalition destroyed Lun, yet Jiong quartered troops outside the capital, ruled tyrannically, and was killed the next year.
value.literal: At that time Prince Qi Jiong raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun; Lun was destroyed, but Jiong kept his army from court, monopolized power, and indulged in arrogance and luxury; the next year he was executed.

value.zh: 惠帝元康五年四月，有星孛於奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、太陵。
value.en: Yuan-kang 5 comet crossed capital stars.
value.literal: In Yuan-kang 5 fourth month a broom star appeared in Striding Legs reaching Chariot and Supreme Palace crossing Three Steps and Great Mound.

value.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子庭，三台為三司，太陵有積尸死喪之事。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Legs is Lu and also arsenal troops; Xuanyuan is the rear palace; the Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven’s court; the Three Terraces are the Three Offices; Great Mound has affairs of piled corpses, death, and mourning."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Striding Legs is Lu and armory stores; Chariot Shaft is harem; Supreme Palace the court; Three Steps the Three Dukes; Great Mound holds piled corpses and death.

value.zh: 其後武庫火，西羌反。
value.en: Armory fire and Qiang revolt.
value.literal: Afterward the arsenal burned and Qiang rebelled west.

value.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。
value.en: Later Zhang Hua and Jia clan fell.
value.literal: Five years later Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and killed; Duke Lu Jia Mi executed.

value.zh: 又明年，趙王倫篡位。
value.en: Next year Sima Lun seized throne.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped.

value.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，兵士戰死十餘萬人。
value.en: Princely coalition slaughtered tens of thousands.
value.literal: Then the Three Princes rose against Lun—over a hundred thousand soldiers died.

value.zh: 永康元年三月，妖星見南方。
value.en: Yongkang 1 March southern astral demon.
value.literal: In Yongkang 1 third month an evil star appeared in the south.

value.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "When a baleful star emerges, great war under Heaven is about to arise."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When evil stars emerge great armies will arise.

value.zh: 是月賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后，斬司空張華，又廢帝自立。
value.en: Jia killed heir; Lun purged court.
value.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered her, executed Zhang Hua, and enthroned himself.

value.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總天權。
value.en: Princes vied for power.
value.literal: Then three princes rose, trading supreme authority.

value.zh: 其十二月，彗星出牽牛之西，指天市。
value.en: December comet Herdsman to market.
value.literal: That twelfth month a comet emerged west of Herdsman pointing at Celestial Market.

value.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。
value.en: The prognostication said, "Ox is the beginning of the seven regulators; when a comet emerges from it, it is the image of changing the era and altering the title.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Ox begins the seven regulators; a comet there means changing era and reign title.

value.zh: 天市一名天府，一名天子旗，帝坐在其中。」
value.en: The Celestial Market is also called the Celestial Treasury and also the Son of Heaven’s Banner; the imperial seat is within it."
value.literal: Celestial Market is also called Celestial Treasury and Son of Heaven’s banner—the throne sits within.

value.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。
value.en: Lun’s coup collapsed.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped, changed the era, then fell to great armies.

value.zh: 二年四月，彗星見齊分。
value.en: Year two April Qi comet.
value.literal: In the second year’s fourth month a comet appeared in Qi field.

value.zh: 占曰：「齊有兵喪。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Qi will have war and mourning."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Qi will suffer armies and mourning.

value.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫。
value.en: Qi prince attacked Lun.
value.literal: Then Prince Qi Jiong rose against Prince Zhao Lun.

value.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢。
value.en: Jiong tyrannized Luoyang.
value.literal: After Lun fell Jiong kept armies outside court, monopolizing power in arrogance and luxury.

value.zh: 明年，誅死。
value.en: Jiong executed next year.
value.literal: The next year he was executed.

value.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
value.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
value.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

value.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
value.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
value.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

value.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
value.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
value.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

value.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
value.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
value.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

value.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
value.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
value.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

value.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
value.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
value.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

value.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
value.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
value.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

value.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
value.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
value.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

value.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
value.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
value.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

value.zh: 安豐太守程諒先已有妻，後又娶，遂立二嫡。
value.en: Cheng Liang, prefect of Anfeng, already had a wife, then married again, thus setting up two principals.'
value.literal: Cheng Liang, prefect of Anfeng, already had a wife, then married again, thus setting up two principals.'

value.zh: 前妻亡，後妻子勳疑所服。
value.en: When the first wife died, the later wife's son Xun doubted what to wear.'
value.literal: When the first wife died, the later wife's son Xun doubted what to wear.'

value.zh: 中書令張華造甲乙之問曰：「甲娶乙為妻，後又娶丙，匿不說有乙，居家如二嫡，無有貴賤之差。
value.en: Prefect of the Masters of Writing Zhang Hua posed a paired question: "A took B as wife, later took C, hiding that B existed—he lived as if with two principals of equal rank.
value.literal: Prefect of the Masters of Writing Zhang Hua posed a paired question: "A took B as wife, later took C, hiding that B existed—he lived as if with two principals of equal rank.

value.zh: 乙亡，丙之子當何服？
value.en: When B died, what should C's son wear?
value.literal: When B died, what should C's son wear?

value.zh: 本實並列，嫡庶不殊，雖二嫡非正，此失在先人，人子何得專制析其親也。
value.en: In truth both stood coequal; principal and secondary were not distinguished—though two principals are irregular, the fault lies with the elders; how may a child on his own sever kin!
value.literal: In truth both stood coequal; principal and secondary were not distinguished—though two principals are irregular, the fault lies with the elders; how may a child on his own sever kin!

value.zh: 若為庶母服，又不成為庶。
value.en: If he wears mourning for a concubine-mother, he cannot really be a concubine son.
value.literal: If he wears mourning for a concubine-mother, he cannot really be a concubine son.

value.zh: 進退不知所從。」
value.en: He cannot decide whether to advance or retreat.'
value.literal: He cannot decide whether to advance or retreat.'

value.zh: 太傅鄭沖議曰：「甲失禮於家，二嫡並在，誠非人子所得正。
value.en: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong answered: "A failed ritual at home—two principals present—is not something a child may correct.
value.literal: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong answered: "A failed ritual at home—two principals present—is not something a child may correct.

value.zh: 則乙丙之子並當三年，禮疑從重。」
value.en: Then sons of both B and C should wear three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.'
value.literal: Then sons of both B and C should wear three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.'

value.zh: 車騎賈充、侍中少傅任愷議略與鄭同。
value.en: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai largely agreed with Zheng.'
value.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai largely agreed with Zheng.'

value.zh: 太尉荀顗議曰：「《春秋》並后匹嫡，古之明典也。
value.en: Grand Commandant Xun Yi answered: "The Spring and Autumn treats two coequal empresses as a clear mirror of error.
value.literal: Grand Commandant Xun Yi answered: "The Spring and Autumn treats two coequal empresses as a clear mirror of error.

value.zh: 今不可以犯禮並立二妻，不別尊卑而遂其失也。
value.en: Today one cannot break ritual to keep two wives; one must not blur noble and base and perpetuate the fault.
value.literal: Today one cannot break ritual to keep two wives; one must not blur noble and base and perpetuate the fault.

value.zh: 故當斷之以禮，先至為嫡，後至為庶。
value.en: Therefore ritual must decide: first arrival is principal, later is secondary.
value.literal: Therefore ritual must decide: first arrival is principal, later is secondary.

value.zh: 丙子宜以嫡母服乙，乙子宜以庶母事丙。
value.en: C's son should mourn B as principal mother; B's son should serve C as secondary mother.
value.literal: C's son should mourn B as principal mother; B's son should serve C as secondary mother.

value.zh: 昔屈建去芰，古人以為違禮而得禮。
value.en: Formerly Qu Jian cast aside water caltrop—ancients thought him wrong on the letter yet right on ritual.
value.literal: Formerly Qu Jian cast aside water caltrop—ancients thought him wrong on the letter yet right on ritual.

value.zh: 丙子非為抑其親，斯自奉禮先後貴賤順敘之義也。」
value.en: C's son is not belittling kin—he follows the sequence of ritual precedence.'
value.literal: C's son is not belittling kin—he follows the sequence of ritual precedence.'

value.zh: 中書監荀勖議曰：「昔鄉里鄭子群娶陳司空從妹，後隔呂布之亂，不復相知存亡，更娶鄉里蔡氏女。
value.en: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu answered: "Formerly Zheng Ziqun of the village married a cousin of Director Chen; later, separated by Lu Bu's chaos, he could not learn whether she lived, and remarried a Cai woman in the village.
value.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu answered: "Formerly Zheng Ziqun of the village married a cousin of Director Chen; later, separated by Lu Bu's chaos, he could not learn whether she lived, and remarried a Cai woman in the village.

value.zh: 徐州平定，陳氏得還，遂二妃並存。
value.en: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen lady returned—then both consorts coexisted.
value.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen lady returned—then both consorts coexisted.

value.zh: 蔡氏之子字元釁，為陳氏服嫡母之服，事陳公以從舅之禮。
value.en: The Cai son, styled Yuanxin, wore principal mourning for the Chen lady and served Director Chen by the courtesy due a maternal uncle.
value.literal: The Cai son, styled Yuanxin, wore principal mourning for the Chen lady and served Director Chen by the courtesy due a maternal uncle.

value.zh: 族兄宗伯曾責元釁，謂抑其親，鄉里先達以元釁為合宜。
value.en: A senior kinsman once reproached Yuanxin for belittling kin, yet village worthies approved him.
value.literal: A senior kinsman once reproached Yuanxin for belittling kin, yet village worthies approved him.

value.zh: 不審此事粗相似否。」，
value.en: He asked whether the present case is broadly similar.'
value.literal: He asked whether the present case is broadly similar.'

value.zh: 樂志上
value.en: Treatise on Music: Part One
value.literal: Music Treatise, Part One

value.zh: 武皇帝采漢魏之遺范，覽景文之垂則，鼎鼐唯新，前音不改。
value.en: Jin’s Emperor Wu took Han–Wei patterns as his mold, reviewed precedents left by Emperors Jing and Wen, replaced the ritual vessels, yet kept the older musical substance intact.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin adopted Han and Wei survivals, surveyed the lasting norms left by Jing and Wen, renewed the tripod vessels of state, yet left earlier musical substance unchanged.

value.zh: 泰始九年，光祿大夫荀勖始作古尺，以調聲韻，仍以張華等所制高文，陳諸下管。
value.en: In the ninth year of Taishi, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Xun Xu first fashioned ancient foot-rules to tune intervals, then still employed the majestic pieces Zhang Hua’s circle had written, presenting them beneath the standing pipes.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, Minister Guanglu Xun Xu first fashioned ancient foot-rules to regulate modes and pitches, then still employed the lofty compositions by Zhang Hua and others, presenting them beneath the pipes.

value.zh: 永嘉之亂，伶官既減，曲台宣榭，咸變汙萊。
value.en: The Yongjia disaster wiped out entire corps of musicians; Pattern Terrace and shuttered galleries alike turned to muddy ruin.
value.literal: When the Yongjia turmoil struck, music officers were decimated; Terrace of Patterns and leaf-screened galleries alike sank into weed-choked wastes.

value.zh: 雖復《象舞》歌工，自胡歸晉，至於孤竹之管，雲和之瑟，空桑之琴，泗濱之磬，其能備者，百不一焉。
value.en: Even after “Elephant” dancers and choristers came south from the Hu domains, sets pairing Guzhu flutes, Yunhe zithers, hollow-sang lutes, and Siban stones survived intact perhaps once in a hundred cases.
value.literal: Though dancers for the “Elephant” dance and singing craftsmen returned from the northern tribes to Jin, as for Guzhu pipes, Yunhe zithers, hollow-sang lutes, and Siban chimes, scarcely one ensemble in a hundred remained complete.

value.zh: 夫人受天地之靈，蘊菁華之氣，剛柔遞用，哀樂分情。
value.en: People inherit Heaven and Earth’s spiritual charge and store its distilled brilliance; yielding and firm forces trade places in turn, while sorrow and joy partition the heart.
value.literal: Human beings receive the subtle powers of Heaven and Earth and harbor the condensed essence of brilliant vigor; hardness and softness alternate in application, grief and joy divide the feelings.

value.zh: 經春陽而自喜，遇秋雕而不悅。
value.en: Spring sunlight lifts them without prompting; autumn’s frost chills their mood unbidden.
value.literal: Passing through spring sunshine they rejoice of themselves; meeting autumn’s stripping frost they lose cheer.

value.zh: 游乎金石之端，出乎管弦之外，因物遷逝，乘流不反。
value.en: They wander where bells and stones fade into silence and drift beyond strings and winds; as circumstance turns, feeling rides the current and never reverses.
value.literal: They roam at the boundary of metal and stone, sail beyond strings and pipes; things shift with circumstance and time drifts downstream without turning back.

value.zh: 是以楚王升輕軒于彭蠡，漢順聽鳴鳥于樊衢。
value.en: So the Chu king raced his light car beside Pengli marsh, while Emperor Shundi of Han lingered over birdsong where Fan’s highways crossed.
value.literal: Thus the king of Chu boarded his light carriage by Peng Lake, and Emperor Shun of Han listened to singing birds along the lanes of Fan.

value.zh: 聖人功成作樂，化平裁曲，乃揚節奏，以暢中和，飾其歡欣，止於哀思者也。
value.en: So the sage, achievements sealed and customs evenly ruled, fashions music and trims tunes—raising rhythm to release inner equipoise, heightening delight yet stopping short of mere lament.
value.literal: Therefore when sages complete their work they create music; when transformation is balanced they trim melodies—only then do they lift beats and measures to vent centered harmony, adorn joy, and halt at mourning-thought.

value.zh: 杜夔傳舊雅樂四曲，一曰《鹿鳴》，二曰《騶虞》，三曰《伐檀》，四曰《文王》，皆古聲辭。
value.en: Du Kui handed down four former elegant-music pieces—“Deer Call,” “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—each preserving archaic lyrics and melody.
value.literal: Du Kui transmitted former ritual music in four pieces—first “Deer Call,” second “Zouyu,” third “Cutting Sandalwood,” fourth “King Wen”—all antique tunes and texts.

value.zh: 及太和中，左延年改夔《騶虞》、《伐檀》、《文王》三曲，更自作聲節，其名雖存，而聲實異。
value.en: Mid-Taihe saw Zuo Yannian rework Du Kui’s settings for “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen,” drafting new beats under old names so hearing no longer matched tradition.
value.literal: By mid-Taihe, Zuo Yannian revised three of Du Kui’s pieces—“Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—making fresh rhythmic schemes himself; though titles survived, the actual sound changed.

value.zh: 唯因夔《鹿鳴》，全不改易。
value.en: Only “Deer Call” stayed exactly as Du Kui left it.
value.literal: Only because of Du Kui’s “Deer Call” did they leave it wholly unchanged.

value.zh: 每正旦大會，太尉奉璧，群後行禮，東廂雅樂常作者是也。
value.en: Thus at each New Year’s dawn court, when the Grand Commandant presents the jade disk and regional lords perform the rites, the elegant ensemble of the eastern wing regularly performs these pieces.
value.literal: Hence at each New Year’s court assembly, when the Grand Commandant presents the jade disk and regional lords perform ritual, the ritual music regularly performed from the eastern wing is this repertoire.

value.zh: 後又改三篇之行禮詩。
value.en: Later they again altered the three ceremonial procession poems.
value.literal: Later they again altered the three procession hymns used during ritual.

value.zh: 第一日《於赫篇》，詠武帝，聲節與古《鹿鳴》同。
value.en: Piece one, “How Radiant,” hymned Emperor Wu to the old meter of “Deer Call.”
value.literal: The first they titled “How Radiant”—praising Emperor Wu—its rhythm matched the ancient “Deer Call.”

value.zh: 第二曰《巍巍篇》，詠文帝，用延年所改《騶虞》聲。
value.en: Piece two, “How Towering,” praised Emperor Wen with Zuo Yannian’s revised “Zouyu” tune.
value.literal: The second they titled “How Towering”—praising Emperor Wen—using the sound Zuo Yannian had refashioned for “Zouyu.”

value.zh: 第三日《洋洋篇》，詠明帝，用延年所改《文王》聲。
value.en: Piece three, “How Vast,” honored Emperor Ming with Zuo Yannian’s altered “King Wen” accompaniment.
value.literal: The third they titled “How Vast”—praising Emperor Ming—using the sound Zuo Yannian had refashioned for “King Wen.”

value.zh: 第四曰復用《鹿鳴》。
value.en: The fourth slot reused “Deer Call” outright.
value.literal: The fourth returned to employing “Deer Call.”

value.zh: 《鹿鳴》之聲重用，而除古《伐檀》。
value.en: Doubling “Deer Call” pushed out archaic “Cutting Sandalwood.”
value.literal: Because “Deer Call” was employed twice, they dropped the ancient “Cutting Sandalwood.”

value.zh: 及晉初，食舉亦用《鹿鳴》。
value.en: Early Jin court dinners still opened with “Deer Call.”
value.literal: When Jin began, banquets at imperial meals likewise used “Deer Call.”

value.zh: 至泰始五年，尚書奏，使太僕傅玄、中書監荀勖、黃門侍郎張華各造正旦行禮及王公上壽酒、食舉樂歌詩。
value.en: In the fifth year of Taishi the Secretariat memorialized, commissioning Minister Coachman Fu Xuan, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, and Imperial Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua each to compose hymn texts for New Year ritual processions, princes' longevity toasts, and meal-accompaniment music.
value.literal: By the fifth year of Taishi the Secretariat memorialized, ordering Minister Coachman Fu Xuan, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, and Imperial Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua each to compose hymn texts for New Year ritual procession, for princes’ longevity toasts, and for meal-accompaniment music.

value.zh: 荀勖云：「魏氏行禮、食舉，再取周詩《鹿鳴》以為樂章。
value.en: Xun Xu argued, “Wei ceremonies and meal ensembles twice lifted Zhou’s ‘Deer Call’ wholesale.
value.literal: Xun Xu stated: “Wei court ritual and meal music twice borrowed Zhou’s ‘Deer Call’ as its lyrics.

value.zh: 又《鹿鳴》以宴嘉賓，無取於朝，考之舊聞，未知所應。」
value.en: Yet ‘Deer Call’ belongs at banquets for noble visitors, not levee halls; antiquity gives no warrant for recycling it here.”
value.literal: Moreover ‘Deer Call’ feasts honored guests—it offers nothing suited to court audiences; reviewing ancient precedent, I cannot see how it fits.”

value.zh: 勖乃除《鹿鳴》舊歌更作行禮詩四篇，先陳三朝朝宗之義。
value.en: So Xun Xu discarded the old “Deer Call” lyrics and composed four procession poems foregrounding the meaning of three-dawn court homage.
value.literal: Xu therefore discarded the old “Deer Call” lyrics and wrote four new procession poems opening with the meaning of three-dawn court homage.

value.zh: 又為正旦大會、王公上壽歌詩並食舉樂歌詩，合十三篇。
value.en: He added lyrics for the dawn levee, royal toast stanzas, and dining suites—thirteen compositions altogether.
value.literal: He further composed hymn texts for the great New Year assembly, princes’ longevity toasts, and meal music—thirteen pieces in all.

value.zh: 又以魏氏歌詩或二言，或三言，或四言，或五言，與古詩不類，以問司律中郎將陳頎。
value.en: Because Wei lyrics varied between two and five syllables unlike classical verse, he queried Pitch Colonel Chen Yi.
value.literal: Moreover because Wei dynasty lyrics sometimes used two, three, four, or five characters per line—unlike ancient poems—he consulted Colonel Director of Pitch Chen Yi.

value.zh: 頎曰：「被之金石，未必皆當。」
value.en: Chen Yi answered, “Fit them to bells and lithophones—not every clause sits equally well.”
value.literal: Yi replied: “Once married to bronze and stone, not every line necessarily fits.”

value.zh: 故勖造晉歌，皆為四言，唯王公上壽酒一篇為三言五言焉。
value.en: Thus Xun Xu’s Jin corpus stays strictly four-beat lines save the longevity stanza mingling triple and quintuple phrases.
value.literal: Hence Xun Xu’s Jin hymns use four-character lines throughout, except one longevity toast mixing three- and five-character verses.

value.zh: 張華以為「魏上壽、食舉詩及漢氏所施用，其文句長短不齊，未皆合古。
value.en: Zhang Hua countered that “Wei toast and banquet lyrics, like Han precedents, stagger line lengths and violate classical meter.
value.literal: Zhang Hua held that “Wei longevity and meal poems plus Han adaptations bear uneven line lengths—not all accord with antiquity.

value.zh: 蓋以依詠弦節，本有因循，而識樂知音，足以制聲度曲，法用率非凡近之所能改。
value.en: They stuck with instrumental phrasing by habit; yet masters who hear true pattern may forge regulated lines—standard practice should not yield to shallow edits.
value.literal: Likely because following string rhythms originally allowed inertia; still, those who grasp music can craft measures and bend tunes—normative usage need not bow to vulgar tinkering.

value.zh: 二代三京，襲而不變，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗留曲折，皆系於舊，有由然也。
value.en: Han and Wei across Luoyang and Ye copied rather than innovated; lyrics rose and fell with politics, yet rhythmic pacing still hugged inherited grooves—and that stubborn continuity had cause.
value.literal: Two dynasties and three capitals inherited without overhaul; although hymn wording shifted with rise and fall of reigns, cadence lingered and turns twisted along old grooves—and therein lay reason.

value.zh: 是以一皆因就，不敢有所改易。」
value.en: So every number hugged precedent—no editor dared novelty."
value.literal: Therefore each piece kept inherited forms—none ventured rash alteration.”

value.zh: 此則華、勖所明異旨也。
value.en: Here Zhang Hua and Xun Xu laid bare how their aims diverged.
value.literal: Thus Zhang Hua and Xun Xu disclosed differing intentions.

value.zh: 時詔又使中書侍郎成公綏亦作焉。
value.en: The court likewise commissioned Secretariat Vice Director Chenggong Sui to supply lyrics.
value.literal: At the same time an edict also ordered Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Chenggong Sui to compose texts.

value.zh: 今並采列之雲。
value.en: What follows preserves both corpora together.
value.literal: Now both sets are excerpted and recorded below.

value.zh: 冬至初歲小會歌張華
value.en: Early-Year Winter-Solstice Gathering Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Minor Assembly Song for Winter Solstice and First Month—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 宴會歌張華
value.en: Convivial Court Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Banquet Song—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 命將出征歌張華
value.en: Marching Host General’s Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Song for Commanders Departing on Campaign—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 重華隆帝道，戎蠻或不賓。
value.en: Chonghua exalted the imperial Way—martial margins sometimes spurned allegiance.
value.literal: Chonghua raised the imperial Way—warlike tribes sometimes refused guesthood.

value.zh: 徐夷興有周，鬼方亦違殷。
value.en: Xu yi stirred under Zhou—Ghost Realm likewise insulted Shang.
value.literal: Xu barbarians rose against Zhou—Guifang likewise defied Yin.

value.zh: 今在盛明世，寇虐動四垠。
value.en: In this brightest reign—raider savagery shakes four rims.
value.literal: Now in this effulgent age—bandit cruelty stirs four borders.

value.zh: 豺狼染牙爪，群生號穹旻。
value.en: Beasts stain teeth and claws—creatures howl at vaulted heaven.
value.literal: Wolves and hounds dye fangs and claws—myriad creatures wail at dome sky.

value.zh: 元帥統方夏，出車撫涼秦。
value.en: Chief commander rules central plain—chariots pacify Liang-Qin marches.
value.literal: Grand marshal commands inner summer—war carts soothe Liang and Qin.

value.zh: 眾貞必以律，臧否實在人。
value.en: United resolve needs measured law—merit judgment lives in human hearts.
value.literal: Mass loyalty must follow statutes—praise or blame truly rests in men.

value.zh: 威信加殊類，疏逖思自親。
value.en: Dread faith reaches stranger tribes—remote minds crave adoption as kin.
value.literal: Prestige and trust touch alien kinds—distant folk wish kinship of themselves.

value.zh: 單醪豈有味，挾纊感至仁。
value.en: One cup of thin brew—no gourmet savor—yet quilted coats feel deepest grace.
value.literal: Single jar of ale—how could it taste sweet?—yet padded coats sense utmost kindness.

value.zh: 武功尚止戈，七德美安民。
value.en: Warrior fame honors ending arms—seven virtues hymn soothing people.
value.literal: Martial merit esteems halting spears—seven powers praise calming folk.

value.zh: 遠跡由斯舉，永世無風塵。
value.en: Distant tracks begin here—endless reign without battle haze.
value.literal: Far footprints rise from this—eternal age without dust of strife.

value.zh: 勞還師歌張華
value.en: Homecoming Host after Punitive March—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Song for Troops Returning from Labor Campaign—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 中宮所歌張華
value.en: Empress Quarter Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Song for the Inner Palace—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 先王統大業，玄化漸八維。
value.en: Ancient sovereigns bound mega-work—subtle reform soaked eight poles.
value.literal: Former kings threaded great enterprise—dark transformation seeped eight dimensions.

value.zh: 儀刑孚萬邦，內訓隆壼闈。
value.en: Pattern and statute swayed all realms—domestic teaching honored queen’s chambers.
value.literal: Model and law won myriad states—inner instruction exalted inner palace.

value.zh: 皇英垂帝典，《大雅》詠三妃。
value.en: Huang and Ying draped dynastic standard—“Greater Ya” hymns three consorts.
value.literal: Huang and Ying hung imperial canon—“Greater Elegantiae” sings three consorts.

value.zh: 執德宣隆教，正位理厥機。
value.en: Clutching merit they spread high doctrine—rightful seat tuned its gears.
value.literal: Grasping virtue they broadcast lofty teaching—correct station ordered its pivots.

value.zh: 含章體柔順，帥禮蹈謙祗。
value.en: With inward pattern they wore yielding grace—guiding ceremony they walked shy reverence.
value.literal: Holding culture they embodied supple obedience—leading ritual they trod humble awe.

value.zh: 《螽斯》弘慈惠，《樛木》逮幽微。
value.en: “Locusts” amplifies mercy—“Tumbling Branch” touches quiet depths.
value.literal: “Locusts” magnifies kindness and grace—“Stooping Bough” reaches hidden subtlety.

value.zh: 徽音穆清風，高義邈不追。
value.en: Bright echoes ride fresh gale—lofty duty beyond chasing.
value.literal: Fine voices breeze clear wind—high righteousness far beyond pursuit.
